# Sendly MCP tools

Generated by `scripts/generate-ai-reference.ts` from `packages/mcp-server/src/tools.ts`.
Do not edit this file by hand. Run `npm run generate:ai-reference` after changing the
source, and `npm run verify:ai-reference` to prove it is still true.

`registerAllTools()` registers **153 tools** across 23 capability areas.
60 are annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, 91 are annotated as writes
(17 of those also carry `destructiveHint: true`), and 2 carry no hint at all.

Every tool calls exactly one Sendly REST endpoint. The endpoint is listed with the tool, so a
tool maps straight onto the HTTP API: the MCP server prefixes `/api/v1` and posts to
`https://sendly.live/api/v1` (`packages/mcp-server/src/api.ts`).

Read the access label as:

- `read-only` safe to call speculatively, changes nothing.
- `write` creates, updates or sends something.
- `write, destructive` also removes or revokes something. Confirm with a human first.
- `unannotated` no `readOnlyHint` in source. Treat as a write.

## Messaging

15 tools.

- **`send_sms`** (write, `POST /api/v1/messages`)
  Send an SMS message to a phone number. Returns the message with delivery status. Use 'transactional' for alerts/OTP (bypasses quiet hours), 'marketing' for promotions.
- **`list_messages`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/messages`)
  List sent and received SMS messages with pagination. Use q parameter for full-text search across message content.
- **`get_message`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/messages/:id`)
  Get details of a specific SMS message including delivery status, timestamps, and metadata.
- **`schedule_sms`** (write, `POST /api/v1/messages/schedule`)
  Schedule an SMS for future delivery (5 minutes to 5 days from now). Credits are reserved immediately and refunded if cancelled.
- **`cancel_scheduled_message`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/messages/scheduled/:id`)
  Cancel a scheduled message before it sends. Credits are refunded automatically.
- **`list_scheduled_messages`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/messages/scheduled`)
  List all scheduled messages that haven't been sent yet.
- **`send_batch`** (write, destructive, `POST /api/v1/messages/batch`)
  Send multiple SMS messages in a single batch (up to 1000). More efficient than individual sends for bulk messaging.
- **`preview_batch`** (read-only, `POST /api/v1/messages/batch/preview`)
  Preview a batch without sending. Returns credit cost estimate and validation results.
- **`get_batch`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/messages/batch/:id`)
  Get the status of a message batch including per-message delivery results.
- **`list_batches`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/messages/batches`)
  List message batches with pagination.
- **`send_group_mms`** (write, `POST /api/v1/messages/group`)
  Send a group MMS to 2-8 US/Canada recipients in one shared thread — everyone sees the others and replies fan out to all participants. Requires the group_mms feature flag (and enable_mms when sending media). Provide 'text' and/or 'mediaUrls'. Defaults to transactional (only an explicit marketing type is subject to quiet hours). Billed per recipient.
- **`send_whatsapp`** (write, `POST /api/v1/messages`)
  Send a free-form WhatsApp text message. Free-form sends only work inside the 24-hour customer-service window: WhatsApp opens (and resets) the window each time the recipient messages your number, and outside it the send fails with whatsapp_window_closed (422, includes windowExpiredAt). If you get that error — or get_whatsapp_window reports open: false — switch to send_whatsapp_template, which works regardless of the window. In-window free-form messages cost 1 credit. The 'from' number must be WhatsApp-connected (see start_whatsapp_signup) or the send fails with whatsapp_sender_not_connected.
- **`send_whatsapp_template`** (write, `POST /api/v1/messages`)
  Send a pre-approved WhatsApp template message. Templates work regardless of the 24-hour window — this is the only way to start a WhatsApp conversation or reach a contact whose window has closed (prefer send_whatsapp for cheap free-form replies while the window is open). The template must already exist for the sender with status APPROVED: whatsapp_template_not_found (404) if no template matches the sender + name + language, whatsapp_template_not_approved (422, includes templateStatus) if Meta hasn't approved it yet. Priced by template category and destination country (authentication/utility cheapest, marketing highest). Note: Meta currently pauses marketing template delivery to US (+1) recipients.
- **`send_rcs`** (write, `POST /api/v1/messages`)
  Send an RCS text message — branded, verified-sender rich messaging, optionally with tappable suggestion chips (reply and open-URL). Recipients whose device or network doesn't support RCS automatically receive the same text as a plain SMS, billed at SMS rates — chips have no SMS form and are dropped (the response discloses suggestionsDropped: true). The response says what actually happened: channel 'rcs' means native RCS delivery; channel 'sms' with fellBackTo: 'sms' means the SMS fallback was used (use check_rcs_capability to know in advance). Requires a live API key (rcs_requires_live_key — RCS is never sandbox-simulated) and a sendable RCS agent on the workspace (rcs_not_enabled otherwise — register one with the rcs_* registration tools, starting at rcs_get_registration; 'testing' agents reach invited test devices only). If the workspace has more than one agent, pass agentId (rcs_agent_ambiguous otherwise).
- **`send_rcs_card`** (write, `POST /api/v1/messages`)
  Send an RCS rich card — a title, body text, optional image, and optional suggestion chips rendered as a standalone card. Cards have NO SMS form: a recipient whose device doesn't support RCS gets rcs_not_supported_for_recipient (422) instead of a fallback, so use check_rcs_capability first (or send_rcs, whose plain text falls back to SMS automatically). Media must be a public JPEG, PNG, or GIF image URL. Requires a live API key and an RCS agent on the workspace; pass agentId when the workspace has more than one agent (rcs_agent_ambiguous otherwise).

## AI message enhancement

1 tools.

- **`enhance_message`** (unannotated, `POST /api/v1/ai/enhance`)
  AI-enhance a draft SMS for clarity, compliance, and send-readiness. Returns a polished ≤160-char rewrite plus a short explanation of what changed. Pass 'messageType' to steer the rewrite; with no 'text' it generates a suitable message for that type. At least one of 'text' or 'messageType' is required. Falls back to the original text with an empty explanation if AI enhancement is unavailable. Requires the ai_classification feature flag.

## Conversations

11 tools.

- **`list_conversations`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/conversations`)
  List SMS conversation threads ordered by most recent activity. Each conversation groups all messages with a specific phone number.
- **`get_conversation_context`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/conversations/:id/context`)
  Get LLM-ready formatted conversation context. Returns a pre-formatted text string with timestamped messages, AI classification, and business context — ready to paste into a prompt.
- **`get_conversation`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/conversations/:id`)
  Get a conversation thread by ID. Set includeMessages=true to load the message history.
- **`reply_to_conversation`** (write, `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/messages`)
  Send a reply within an existing conversation. The recipient is automatically set from the conversation's phone number.
- **`update_conversation`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/conversations/:id`)
  Update a conversation's metadata or tags. Use metadata for custom key-value data, tags for categorization.
- **`close_conversation`** (write, `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/close`)
  Close a conversation. Closed conversations auto-reopen when a new inbound message arrives.
- **`reopen_conversation`** (write, `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/reopen`)
  Reopen a previously closed conversation, setting its status back to active.
- **`mark_conversation_read`** (write, `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/mark-read`)
  Mark a conversation as read, resetting the unread count to zero.
- **`get_suggested_replies`** (unannotated, `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/suggest-replies`)
  Get AI-generated reply suggestions for a conversation based on message history and context. Returns 2-3 suggested responses with different tones (professional, friendly, concise).
- **`add_conversation_label`** (write, `POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/labels`)
  Add one or more labels to a conversation for categorization.
- **`remove_conversation_label`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/conversations/:id/labels/:id`)
  Remove a label from a conversation.

## Contacts

9 tools.

- **`create_contact`** (write, `POST /api/v1/contacts`)
  Create a contact with phone number and optional name, email, metadata. Contacts can be added to lists for campaigns.
- **`list_contacts`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/contacts`)
  List contacts with optional search and pagination. Search matches name, email, and phone number.
- **`get_contact`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/contacts/:id`)
  Get a contact by ID including their list memberships and metadata.
- **`update_contact`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/contacts/:id`)
  Update a contact's name, email, or metadata. Only provided fields are changed.
- **`delete_contact`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/contacts/:id`)
  Delete a contact by ID. Removes the contact from all lists. Does not delete messages sent to this contact.
- **`mark_contact_valid`** (write, `POST /api/v1/contacts/:id/mark-valid`)
  Clear the invalid flag on a contact so future campaigns include it again. Contacts get auto-flagged as invalid when a send fails with a terminal bad-number error (landline, invalid number) or when a carrier lookup reports they can't receive SMS. Use this when you disagree with the auto-flag.
- **`check_contact_numbers`** (write, `POST /api/v1/contacts/lookup`)
  Trigger a background carrier lookup across contacts. Landlines and other non-SMS-capable numbers are auto-excluded from future campaigns. The lookup runs asynchronously (1-5 minutes). Results populate line_type, carrier_name, and invalid_reason fields on affected contacts. Idempotent: re-triggering while a lookup is running for the same scope is a no-op — response carries alreadyRunning: true in that case.
- **`bulk_mark_contacts_valid`** (write, `POST /api/v1/contacts/bulk-mark-valid`)
  Clear the invalid flag on many contacts at once (up to 10,000 per call). Pass either an explicit id array OR a listId — not both. Foreign ids silently no-op via the per-organization filter. Returns { cleared } — the number of contacts whose flag was actually cleared.
- **`import_contacts`** (write, destructive, `POST /api/v1/contacts/import`)
  Bulk import contacts from an array. Optionally add all imported contacts to a list. Returns created/updated/skipped counts.

## Contact lists

7 tools.

- **`create_contact_list`** (write, `POST /api/v1/contact-lists`)
  Create a contact list for organizing contacts and targeting campaigns.
- **`list_contact_lists`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/contact-lists`)
  List all contact lists with their contact counts.
- **`get_contact_list`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/contact-lists/:id`)
  Get a contact list by ID with its members. Use limit/offset to paginate through members.
- **`update_contact_list`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/contact-lists/:id`)
  Update a contact list's name or description.

  Delete a contact list. Contacts in the list are not deleted, only the list grouping is removed.
- **`add_list_contacts`** (write, `POST /api/v1/contact-lists/:id/contacts`)
  Add one or more contacts to a contact list.
- **`remove_list_contact`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/contact-lists/:id/contacts/:id`)
  Remove a single contact from a contact list. The contact itself is not deleted.

## Campaigns

10 tools.

- **`create_campaign`** (write, `POST /api/v1/campaigns`)
  Create a campaign to send bulk SMS to contact lists. Created as a draft — preview and send separately. Supports {{variables}} in message text.
- **`list_campaigns`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/campaigns`)
  List campaigns with optional filtering by status.
- **`get_campaign`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/campaigns/:id`)
  Get a campaign by ID with delivery statistics (sent, delivered, failed counts).
- **`update_campaign`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/campaigns/:id`)
  Update a campaign's name, text, or target list. Only draft and scheduled campaigns can be updated.
- **`delete_campaign`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/campaigns/:id`)
  Delete a campaign. Only draft and cancelled campaigns can be deleted.
- **`preview_campaign`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/campaigns/:id/preview`)
  Preview a campaign before sending. Returns recipient count, estimated credit cost, and whether you have enough credits.
- **`send_campaign`** (write, destructive, `POST /api/v1/campaigns/:id/send`)
  Send a campaign immediately to all recipients in its target lists. Credits are deducted at send time. Preview first to check costs.
- **`schedule_campaign`** (write, `POST /api/v1/campaigns/:id/schedule`)
  Schedule a campaign for future delivery at a specific date and time.
- **`cancel_campaign`** (write, destructive, `POST /api/v1/campaigns/:id/cancel`)
  Cancel a scheduled campaign before it sends. Credits reserved for the campaign are refunded.
- **`clone_campaign`** (write, `POST /api/v1/campaigns/:id/clone`)
  Clone a campaign to create a new draft copy with the same settings. Useful for recurring or A/B campaigns.

## Message templates

8 tools.

- **`create_template`** (write, `POST /api/v1/templates`)
  Create an SMS template with {{variable}} placeholders. Templates can be used with campaigns and the Verify API.
- **`list_templates`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/templates`)
  List all templates (custom and preset) with their status and variable definitions.
- **`get_template`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/templates/:id`)
  Get a template by ID including its variable definitions and publish status.
- **`update_template`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/templates/:id`)
  Update a template's name or text.
- **`delete_template`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/templates/:id`)
  Delete a custom template. Preset templates cannot be deleted.
- **`publish_template`** (write, `POST /api/v1/templates/:id/publish`)
  Publish a template, making it available for use with the Verify API and campaigns.
- **`preview_template`** (read-only, `POST /api/v1/templates/:id/preview`)
  Preview a template with sample variable values to see the interpolated result.
- **`list_template_presets`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/templates/presets`)

## Auto-label rules

4 tools.

- **`list_rules`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/rules`)
  List auto-label rules that automatically tag conversations based on AI-detected intent and sentiment.
- **`create_rule`** (write, `POST /api/v1/rules`)
  Create an auto-label rule. Rules automatically apply labels to conversations when conditions match.
- **`update_rule`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/rules/:id`)

## Drafts

4 tools.

- **`create_draft`** (write, `POST /api/v1/drafts`)
  Create a message draft for human review before sending. The draft must be approved before it becomes a real SMS.
- **`list_drafts`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/drafts`)
  List message drafts, optionally filtered by conversation or status.
- **`approve_draft`** (write, `POST /api/v1/drafts/:id/approve`)
  Approve a pending draft and send it as a real SMS message. Runs compliance checks and deducts credits at approval time.
- **`reject_draft`** (write, `POST /api/v1/drafts/:id/reject`)
  Reject a pending draft with an optional reason. The message will not be sent.

## Webhooks

12 tools.

- **`create_webhook`** (write, `POST /api/v1/webhooks`)
  Create a webhook endpoint to receive real-time event notifications. Returns a signing secret (shown only once) for verifying payloads.
- **`list_webhooks`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/webhooks`)
  List all webhook endpoints with their status and event subscriptions.
- **`get_webhook`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/webhooks/:id`)
  Get a webhook by ID with delivery statistics.
- **`update_webhook`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/:id`)
  Update a webhook's URL, events, description, or active status.
- **`delete_webhook`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/:id`)
  Delete a webhook endpoint. Stops all future event deliveries to this URL.
- **`test_webhook`** (write, `POST /api/v1/webhooks/:id/test`)
  Send a test event to a webhook endpoint to verify it is reachable. Returns response status and latency.
- **`list_webhook_deliveries`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/webhooks/:id/deliveries`)
  Get delivery history for a webhook showing recent attempts, statuses, and response times.
- **`rotate_webhook_secret`** (write, `POST /api/v1/webhooks/:id/rotate-secret`)
  Rotate a webhook's signing secret. The old secret stops working immediately.
- **`list_webhook_event_types`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/webhooks/event-types`)
  List all available webhook event types that can be subscribed to.
- **`reset_webhook_circuit`** (write, `POST /api/v1/webhooks/:id/reset-circuit`)
  Reset the circuit breaker for a webhook so deliveries resume immediately instead of waiting for the automatic 5-minute recovery.
- **`redeliver_webhook`** (write, `POST /api/v1/webhooks/:id/redeliver`)
  Replay failed or cancelled webhook deliveries from the audit log for a time window. Use after a customer endpoint has recovered from an outage. Reset the circuit first if it is open. Each replay preserves the original event_id for dedup.
- **`backfill_webhook`** (write, `POST /api/v1/webhooks/:id/backfill`)
  Synthesize webhook events from the underlying message log for events that have no audit row (the case redeliver_webhook cannot recover). Use this when a circuit-breaker outage left events with no delivery record. Synthesized events have fresh IDs — clients should dedupe by event.data.object.id (the message ID). Reset the circuit first if it is open.

## Verification and OTP

7 tools.

- **`send_otp`** (write, `POST /api/v1/verify`)
  Send an OTP verification code via SMS. Use for phone verification, 2FA, or identity confirmation. In sandbox mode (test API key), the code is returned in the response.
- **`check_otp`** (write, `POST /api/v1/verify/:id/check`)
  Verify an OTP code. Returns 'verified' (correct), 'invalid_code' (wrong), 'expired', or 'max_attempts_exceeded'.
- **`get_verification_status`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/verify/:id`)
  Check the current status of an OTP verification (pending, verified, expired, failed).
- **`resend_otp`** (write, `POST /api/v1/verify/:id/resend`)
  Resend an OTP verification code. Use when the original SMS was not received.
- **`list_verifications`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/verify`)
  List recent OTP verifications with pagination.
- **`create_verify_session`** (write, `POST /api/v1/verify/sessions`)
  Create a hosted verify session with a branded UI. Returns a URL to redirect the user to for phone verification. Zero frontend code needed.
- **`validate_verify_session`** (write, `POST /api/v1/verify/sessions/validate`)
  Validate a session token returned after a user completes hosted verification. Returns the verified phone number.

## Credits

2 tools.

- **`get_credits`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/credits`)
  Get current credit balance including reserved credits for scheduled messages.
- **`list_credit_transactions`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/credits/transactions`)

## Account and API keys

5 tools.

- **`get_account`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/account`)
  Get account info: credit balance, phone number verification status, rate limits, and API key details.
- **`create_api_key`** (write, `POST /api/v1/account/keys`)
  Create a new API key for this account. Returns the raw key exactly once — surface it to the user and tell them to store it securely, it cannot be retrieved again. Live keys require a verified business and a positive credit balance.
- **`list_api_keys`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/account/keys`)
  List the API keys for this account with their id, name, type, prefix, scopes, active state, and last-used time. Raw key values are never returned.
- **`rotate_api_key`** (write, `POST /api/v1/account/keys/:id/rotate`)
  Rotate an API key: generates a replacement key and keeps the old one valid for a grace period (24-168 hours) so you can migrate without downtime. Returns the new raw key exactly once — store it securely. Cannot rotate the key currently in use.
- **`revoke_api_key`** (write, destructive, `PATCH /api/v1/account/keys/:id/revoke`)
  Revoke an API key immediately and permanently. Any request using it will fail afterward. Cannot revoke the key currently in use.

## Short links

3 tools.

- **`shorten_url`** (write, `POST /api/v1/links`)
  Mint a branded short link for a destination URL. Branded owned-domain links improve SMS deliverability (carriers filter public shorteners) and track clicks. Returns { code, shortUrl, destinationUrl }. Gated behind the url_shortener rollout flag — returns 'not_found' until the flag is on for your account.
- **`list_short_links`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/links`)
  List the branded short links this workspace has created, newest first, with click counts, a 14-day daily click histogram (spark), latest country/time, and disabled state.
- **`set_short_link_disabled`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/links/:id`)
  Enable or disable a branded short link (a per-link kill switch). A disabled link's redirect returns 404 until it is re-enabled.

## Enterprise workspaces

4 tools.

- **`generate_business_page`** (write, `POST /api/v1/enterprise/business-page/generate`)
  Generate a hosted business landing page for verification. Returns a URL at sendly.live/biz/{slug}. Enterprise accounts only.
- **`enterprise_workspace_get_verification`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/enterprise/workspaces/:id/verification`)
  Get the current verification record for an enterprise workspace. Useful before submit/resubmit to see what's already on file (the server merges your submit payload with existing fields).
- **`enterprise_workspace_submit_verification`** (write, `POST /api/v1/enterprise/workspaces/:id/verification/submit`)
  Submit or resubmit a toll-free verification for an enterprise workspace. Partial-update friendly: omit fields you don't want to change — they'll be filled from the existing record. Hosted page URLs (/biz/, /opt-in/, /legal/) generated during provision are auto-preserved. For sole proprietors, leave brn/brnType/brnCountry undefined.
- **`enterprise_workspace_resubmit_verification`** (write, `POST /api/v1/enterprise/workspaces/:id/verification/submit`)
  Convenience alias for submit_verification — identical behavior. Use when retrying after a rejection.

## Phone numbers

7 tools.

- **`list_number_countries`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/numbers/countries`)
  List the countries where Sendly phone numbers can be purchased, along with the number types available in each (e.g., mobile, local, toll-free). Use this before search_available_numbers to discover valid country codes and types.
- **`search_available_numbers`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/numbers/available`)
  Search for phone numbers available to purchase in a given country and type. Returns candidates with phoneNumber, country, numberType, and monthlyCost (already customer-priced, a string) plus currency. Use list_number_countries first to find valid country codes and types, then pass a result's phoneNumber + numberType + monthlyCost straight into buy_number.
- **`list_numbers`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/numbers`)
  List the phone numbers owned by your workspace. Each number includes: status (one of provisioning | requirements_required | active | failed — a number can only send/receive once active; note a US local number additionally cannot send until it is assigned to a registered 10DLC campaign, even while status is active), source, country, type, monthlyCostCents, requirementsSubmittedAt (for a requirements_required number: null = still needs regulatory documents, a timestamp = documents submitted and under carrier review), and pendingCancellation / scheduledReleaseAt (set when the number is scheduled for release at the end of its paid period).
- **`get_number`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/numbers/:id`)
  Get one phone number your workspace owns by its Sendly ID. Returns the same fields as list_numbers — status (provisioning | requirements_required | active | failed; only 'active' can send/receive, and a US local number additionally needs assignment to a registered 10DLC campaign before it can send even once active), source, countryCode, phoneNumberType, monthlyCostCents, requirementsSubmittedAt, pendingCancellation, scheduledReleaseAt — plus isDefault (whether it is the workspace's default sender). Returns not_found if the id isn't a number this workspace owns.
- **`buy_number`** (write, `POST /api/v1/numbers/buy`)
  Buy a phone number found via search_available_numbers. Pass a search result's exact phoneNumber, countryCode, phoneNumberType, and monthlyCost. Returns one of four outcomes: 'provisioning' (the number is yours and being set up — poll list_numbers until status is active); 'payment_required' or 'documents_required' (a human step is needed first); or 'under_review' (documents submitted — see below). For payment_required/documents_required the result includes action.url, action.actionCode (a 32-hex identifier), and action.code (a short human-typed code). You (the agent) cannot do this step yourself: relay action.url and action.code to the human and ask them to open the link and either add a card (payment_required) or provide their business details + upload documents (documents_required). After they finish, re-run buy_number with the SAME arguments PLUS actionCode set to action.actionCode (NOT action.code). A documents_required buy then returns 'under_review': the number is reserved and being verified + registered, usually a few business days — it cannot send until active, so poll list_numbers and watch status become active. IMPORTANT for US local numbers: the result may include registrationRequired: true. Such a number WILL reach status 'active' but STILL cannot send a single message until it is assigned to a registered 10DLC campaign — after it goes active, register a brand + campaign with the tendlc_* tools and assign the number with tendlc_assign_number. Never tell the user a registrationRequired number is ready to text; say it is active but must finish 10DLC registration first. Never reveal internal carrier or provider names to the user; refer only to 'the carrier', 'under review', or 'being registered'.
- **`update_number`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/numbers/:id`)
  Update a phone number your workspace owns. Two mutations are supported: pass { isDefault: true } to make it the workspace's default sender (the previous default is cleared atomically; the number must be 'active' or you get invalid_state), and/or { pendingCancellation: false } to undo a scheduled period-end release ('keep this number'). Provide at least one — any other field is rejected with no_supported_fields. Returns the full updated number. not_found if the id isn't a number this workspace owns.
- **`release_number`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/numbers/:id`)
  Release a phone number your workspace owns. For a live paid purchase this schedules cancellation at the end of the current paid period and returns { success: true, scheduled: true, scheduledReleaseAt } (undo it with update_number { pendingCancellation: false }). Otherwise the number is released immediately at the carrier and dropped, returning { success: true }. not_found if the id isn't a number this workspace owns.

## Business upgrade preflight

2 tools.

- **`preflight_business_upgrade`** (read-only, `POST /api/v1/verification/preflight`)
  Validate a proposed business entity upgrade before submitting. Returns issues + auto-fix suggestions (e.g. 'sole-prop + EIN mismatch — change entity to PRIVATE_PROFIT'). Use this to dry-run new entity details before calling start_business_upgrade. Read-only; no DB or carrier writes.
- **`get_business_upgrade_best_prefill`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/verification/best-prefill`)
  Read 'best-of' values for the upgrade form across all of the caller's verified workspaces. Returns most-recent non-empty values per messaging field (useCase, sampleMessages, optInWorkflow, etc.). Useful when populating a fresh upgrade form for a workspace whose current record is incomplete.

## Business entity upgrade

5 tools.

- **`start_business_upgrade`** (write, `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:id/upgrade`)
  Start a business entity upgrade for the given workspace. Auto-provisions a new toll-free number + messaging profile under the new entity, submits to the carrier for review, and stores the EIN document (if provided) securely until approval. The current toll-free number keeps sending throughout the 1-2 week review window; on approval, the new number takes over atomically. Use preflight_business_upgrade first to surface any blockers.
- **`get_business_upgrade_status`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:id/upgrade/status`)
  Check the status of a pending business entity upgrade for a workspace. Returns the pending row (with status, target toll-free number, rejection reason if any) or null if no upgrade is in flight. Statuses: provisioning, pending, in_progress, processing, action_required, rejected, verified.
- **`cancel_business_upgrade`** (write, destructive, `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:id/upgrade/cancel`)
  Cancel a pending business entity upgrade. Releases the reserved toll-free number, deletes the new messaging profile, removes the stored EIN document, and clears the pending record. The current toll-free number is unaffected. Idempotent — returns success even if there was nothing to cancel.
- **`resubmit_business_upgrade`** (write, `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:id/upgrade/resubmit`)
  Resubmit a previously rejected (or waiting-for-customer) business entity upgrade with corrected fields and optionally a new EIN document. Same field shape as start_business_upgrade; fields you omit keep the previously-submitted values.
- **`set_business_upgrade_old_number_disposition`** (write, `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:id/upgrade/disposition`)
  After a successful business upgrade, choose what happens to the old (now-superseded) toll-free number. 'moved' keeps it active under another workspace owned by the same user (requires targetWorkspaceId); 'released' returns it to the carrier pool. Idempotent.

## 10DLC brands and campaigns

9 tools.

- **`tendlc_list_brands`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/tendlc/brands`)
  List the workspace's 10DLC brands registered for carrier review. A brand is the business identity behind local-number texting; each entry includes status (pending | verified | failed), identityStatus, and failureReasons when carrier review rejected it. Check this before tendlc_create_brand to avoid registering a duplicate.
- **`tendlc_create_brand`** (write, `POST /api/v1/tendlc/brands`)
  Register a 10DLC brand for carrier review — step 1 of enabling texting from local numbers. Review is asynchronous: the brand is returned with status 'pending'; poll tendlc_get_brand until it becomes 'verified' (then create a campaign) or 'failed' (see failureReasons). Requires a live API key; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`tendlc_get_brand`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/tendlc/brands/:id`)
  Get one 10DLC brand by ID. Fetching also refreshes the brand's carrier-review status server-side, so poll this tool to track progress (pending → verified/failed). Once verified, the brand can host campaigns via tendlc_create_campaign.
- **`tendlc_qualify_usecase`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/tendlc/brands/:id/qualify/:id`)
  Pre-check whether a use case qualifies for a brand on the carrier network before creating a campaign. Returns qualified (boolean), a reason when not qualified, and the expected throughput tier ('High volume' | 'Standard' | 'Low volume') with the number of carriers ready. Run this after the brand is verified and before tendlc_create_campaign to avoid a failed submission.
- **`tendlc_list_campaigns`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/tendlc/campaigns`)
  List the workspace's 10DLC messaging campaigns. Each entry includes status (pending | active | failed | suspended | expired), useCase, sampleMessages, throughput (tier + carriersReady, once carriers approve), and failureReasons when carrier review rejected it. Numbers can only be assigned to campaigns with status 'active'.
- **`tendlc_create_campaign`** (write, `POST /api/v1/tendlc/campaigns`)
  Create a 10DLC messaging campaign under a verified brand and submit it for carrier review — step 2 of enabling local-number texting. The brand must have status 'verified' first (use tendlc_qualify_usecase to pre-check the use case). Review is asynchronous: the campaign starts 'pending'; poll tendlc_get_campaign until it becomes 'active', then assign a number with tendlc_assign_number. Requires a live API key; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`tendlc_get_campaign`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/tendlc/campaigns/:id`)
  Get one 10DLC campaign by ID. Fetching also refreshes the campaign's carrier-review status server-side, so poll this tool to track progress (pending → active), including throughput (tier + carriersReady) once carriers approve. On 'failed', check failureReasons.
- **`tendlc_assign_number`** (write, `POST /api/v1/tendlc/campaigns/:id/assign`)
  Assign a workspace-owned phone number to an active (carrier-approved) 10DLC campaign — step 3, this makes the number sendable. The campaign must have status 'active' and the number must already belong to the workspace (see list_numbers). Idempotent: re-assigning the same number to the same campaign returns the existing assignment. A number can only be on one campaign at a time (409 number_already_assigned otherwise). Requires a live API key; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`tendlc_list_assignments`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/tendlc/assignments`)
  List the workspace's number-to-campaign assignments. Each entry includes campaignId, phoneNumber, status ('Active' | 'Under review' | 'Action needed'), and assignedAt. Use this to confirm which numbers are cleared to send via 10DLC.

## WhatsApp channel

10 tools.

- **`start_whatsapp_signup`** (write, `POST /api/v1/whatsapp/signup`)
  Connect a workspace phone number to WhatsApp so it can send and receive WhatsApp messages. Returns { id, connectUrl, status }. You (the agent) CANNOT complete this step yourself: connectUrl opens a browser flow that requires the business owner to log in with Facebook and link their WhatsApp Business account. Relay connectUrl to the human, ask them to open it and finish connecting, then poll get_whatsapp_signup_status with the returned id. A one-time $19 setup fee is charged when the connection succeeds; there is no monthly WhatsApp fee.
- **`get_whatsapp_signup_status`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/whatsapp/signup/:id`)
  Get the status of a WhatsApp signup started with start_whatsapp_signup. Returns { id, status, phoneNumber, businessAccountId, failureReasons, updatedAt }. Poll this after the human has completed the connectUrl browser step. Once status reaches active the number can send via send_whatsapp / send_whatsapp_template; on failed, failureReasons says what to fix.
- **`list_whatsapp_senders`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/whatsapp/senders`)
  List the workspace's WhatsApp senders — the numbers connected (or connecting) to WhatsApp — newest first. Each entry includes phoneNumber, displayName (null until one is set during the connect flow), status (pending | active | suspended), qualityRating (Meta's quality signal, null until Meta reports one), and createdAt. Only active senders can send via send_whatsapp / send_whatsapp_template. An empty list means no number is WhatsApp-connected yet — connect one with start_whatsapp_signup.
- **`get_whatsapp_sender_profile`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/whatsapp/senders/:id/profile`)
  Get the WhatsApp business profile customers see for a connected sender number. Returns { phoneNumber, displayName, profilePhotoUrl, category, about, description, email, website, address } (fields the business hasn't set are null). The number must be an active WhatsApp sender — whatsapp_sender_not_connected (404) otherwise (see list_whatsapp_senders). The profile is fetched live from the carrier, so whatsapp_profile_fetch_failed (502) is transient — retry shortly.
- **`update_whatsapp_sender_profile`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/whatsapp/senders/:id/profile`)
  Update the WhatsApp business profile customers see for a connected sender number — the details shown when someone taps the business name in WhatsApp. Provide only the fields to change; at least one is required. Returns the updated profile ({ phoneNumber, displayName, profilePhotoUrl, category, about, description, email, website, address }). The number must be an active WhatsApp sender — whatsapp_sender_not_connected (404) otherwise. The write goes through to the carrier, so whatsapp_profile_update_failed (502) is transient — retry shortly. Requires a live API key.
- **`list_whatsapp_templates`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/whatsapp/templates`)
  List the workspace's WhatsApp message templates. Each entry includes id, name, language, category (authentication | utility | marketing), status (PENDING | APPROVED | REJECTED | PAUSED | DISABLED), and rejection details when Meta rejected it. Only APPROVED templates can be sent with send_whatsapp_template. Poll this after create_whatsapp_template or update_whatsapp_template to track Meta review (typically 24-48h).
- **`create_whatsapp_template`** (write, `POST /api/v1/whatsapp/templates`)
  Create a WhatsApp message template and submit it for Meta review (typically 24-48h — poll list_whatsapp_templates for the verdict). Approved templates are the only way to message outside the 24-hour window. Body text uses numbered placeholders {{1}}, {{2}}, … and EVERY placeholder must have a matching entry in examples, or creation is rejected. Template names are locked for ~30 days once submitted (even after deletion): if Meta rejects a template, fix it with update_whatsapp_template instead of creating a new one under a different name.
- **`update_whatsapp_template`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/whatsapp/templates/:id`)
  Edit a WhatsApp template and resubmit it for Meta review. Only templates with status APPROVED or REJECTED can be edited — this is the escape from Meta's ~30-day template-name lock: when a template is REJECTED, fix it here and resubmit under the same name instead of waiting a month to reuse it. Editing sends the template back through Meta review (typically 24-48h; poll list_whatsapp_templates). PENDING, PAUSED, and DISABLED templates cannot be edited. Provide only the fields to change.
- **`delete_whatsapp_template`** (write, destructive, `DELETE /api/v1/whatsapp/templates/:id`)
  Delete a WhatsApp message template. Returns { id, deleted: true }. Think twice before deleting: Meta reserves a deleted template's name for up to 30 days, so a rejected template should be fixed with update_whatsapp_template and resubmitted under the same name rather than deleted and re-created. Requires a live API key.
- **`get_whatsapp_window`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/whatsapp/window`)
  Check whether the 24-hour WhatsApp customer-service window between a sender and a recipient is currently open. Returns { open, expiresAt }. Call this before send_whatsapp to avoid a failed send: open true means free-form messages are allowed until expiresAt; open false means only templates deliver — use send_whatsapp_template. The window opens (and resets to 24 hours) every time the recipient messages the sender on WhatsApp.

## RCS channel

12 tools.

- **`list_rcs_agents`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/rcs/agents`)
  List the workspace's RCS agents — the branded sender identities RCS messages go out from — newest first. Each entry includes id, name, status, useCase, sendable, stage, and createdAt. sendable true means the agent can send right now: 'testing' agents reach invited test devices only, 'approved' agents reach everyone. stage is where the agent's registration sits (draft | in_review | changes_requested | rejected | brand_verification | agent_review | testing | launch_review | launching | launch_rejected | live | suspended | failed); use rcs_get_agent for the detail behind it. An empty list means no agent has been registered yet — register one with the rcs_* registration tools, starting at rcs_get_registration (Sendly reviews the registration, then the carrier network verifies it). Error not_found means RCS isn't enabled for this account yet — the account owner can ask Sendly support.
- **`check_rcs_capability`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/rcs/capability`)
  Check whether a recipient's device and network can receive RCS before sending. Returns { to, agentId, capable, features }. capable true means send_rcs delivers natively and send_rcs_card will work; capable false means send_rcs falls back to plain SMS and send_rcs_card fails with rcs_not_supported_for_recipient. Requires a live API key (rcs_requires_live_key on test keys — the probe queries the carrier network). Pass agentId when the workspace has more than one agent.
- **`rcs_get_registration`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/rcs/registration`)
  Get the workspace's RCS registration at a glance — the brand (business identity), the newest agent (the branded sender), that agent's invited test devices, the overall stage, and usEligible. Start here before any other rcs_* registration tool. stage tells you what to do next: 'draft' — fill in with rcs_create_brand and rcs_create_agent, then rcs_submit_registration; 'in_review' — Sendly is reviewing it, nothing to do; 'changes_requested' — read brand.reviewNote / agent.reviewNote, fix with rcs_update_brand / rcs_update_agent, then rcs_submit_registration again; 'brand_verification' / 'agent_review' — the carrier network is reviewing it, wait; 'testing' — invite phones with rcs_set_test_devices, complete the campaign with rcs_update_agent, then rcs_request_launch; 'launch_review' / 'launching' — wait; 'launch_rejected' — see agent.rejectionReason, fix, then rcs_request_launch again; 'live' — the agent sends with send_rcs; 'rejected' / 'failed' — see reviewNote / rejectionReason. brand and agent are null until created. Error rcs_not_enabled means RCS registration isn't enabled for this account yet — the account owner can ask Sendly support. Read-only; requires the rcs:read scope (on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit reading verifications).
- **`rcs_get_dossier`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/rcs/dossier`)
  Prefill for a new RCS brand: the business details Sendly already has on file for this workspace, returned as a partial brand — legalName, displayName, ein, organizationType, websiteUrl, address, contact — plus source ('tendlc' when taken from the workspace's 10DLC brand, 'verification' from its toll-free verification, 'none' when nothing is on file) and usEligible. Call this before rcs_create_brand, confirm the details with the human, fill the gaps, and pass the result as the brand. usEligible false means something on file names a non-US country, and the brand will be refused (rcs_us_only). Read-only; requires the rcs:read scope.
- **`rcs_create_brand`** (write, `POST /api/v1/rcs/brands`)
  Draft the RCS brand — the business identity behind a branded sender — step 1 of RCS registration. Only the country is checked here (address.countryCode must be 'US'; rcs_us_only otherwise): the required fields — displayName, legalName, legalEntityType, organizationType, websiteUrl, ein, a full address, and a full contact — are validated at rcs_submit_registration, so you can draft with partial details and finish with rcs_update_brand. Use rcs_get_dossier first to prefill what Sendly already knows. Returns { brand } with reviewStatus 'draft'; keep brand.id for rcs_create_agent. One brand is enough for a workspace — check rcs_get_registration before creating another. Requires the rcs:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`rcs_update_brand`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/rcs/brands/:id`)
  Patch a draft RCS brand. Only the keys you pass change; null clears a nullable field; address and contact may be partial objects. Editable while brand.reviewStatus is 'draft' or 'changes_requested' (brand.reviewNote says what Sendly asked for); rcs_field_locked (409) while it's awaiting review, while a launch is requested, and once the brand has gone to the carrier network. address.countryCode, if passed, must be 'US' (rcs_us_only otherwise). rcs_not_found when the ID isn't in this workspace. Returns { brand }. Requires the rcs:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`rcs_create_agent`** (write, `POST /api/v1/rcs/agents`)
  Draft the RCS agent — the branded sender identity recipients see — under a brand, step 2 of RCS registration. Pass brandId (from rcs_create_brand or rcs_get_registration) plus what you know: displayName (max 40 characters), useCase (MULTI_USE | PROMOTIONAL | TRANSACTIONAL | OTP), and basics (description, logo, hero, brand colour, privacy policy and terms URLs, and at least one phone/website/email contact). Completeness is enforced at rcs_submit_registration, so drafting with partial details is fine; the campaign (what you message about, examples, consent) and testing sections can wait until the agent reaches the 'testing' stage. Logo, hero, and call-to-action media must already be public https:// URLs — assets can't be uploaded over the API (rcs_invalid_content otherwise; the dashboard can upload them). rcs_not_found when the brand isn't in this workspace. Returns { agent } with reviewStatus 'draft' and an empty testDevices list; keep agent.id. Requires the rcs:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`rcs_get_agent`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/rcs/agents/:id`)
  Get one RCS agent by ID with its test devices and stage — poll this to follow a registration. Returns { agent, devices, stage }. agent.reviewStatus is Sendly's review state (draft | awaiting_review | changes_requested | approved_for_carrier | rejected | launch_requested | launch_submitted | launch_rejected | failed); stage (also agent.customerStage) is the plain-language position: draft → in_review → brand_verification → agent_review → testing → launch_review → launching → live, with changes_requested, rejected, launch_rejected, suspended, and failed as side exits. agent.reviewNote is what Sendly asked for; agent.rejectionReason is what the carrier network said. rcs_not_found when the ID isn't in this workspace. Read-only; requires the rcs:read scope.
- **`rcs_update_agent`** (write, `PATCH /api/v1/rcs/agents/:id`)
  Patch a draft RCS agent. Sections are merged: displayName, useCase, and basics patch the basics group; campaign and testing are merged key by key; campaign: null or testing: null clears that whole section. Editable while agent.reviewStatus is 'draft' or 'changes_requested' (agent.reviewNote says what Sendly asked for); rcs_field_locked (409) while it's awaiting review or a launch is requested — and once the basics have gone to the carrier network they're locked, so from the 'testing' stage on only campaign and testing change. Use it at the 'testing' stage to complete the campaign before rcs_request_launch: companyOverview and agentOverview, at least 1 interaction, at least 3 messageExamples (include STOP and HELP wording), and consentSettings with at least 1 optInMethod, callToAction, doubleOptIn true/false, optInMessage, helpResponse, and optOutResponse. Media URLs must be public https:// (assets can't be uploaded over the API). rcs_not_found when the ID isn't in this workspace. Returns { agent }. Requires the rcs:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`rcs_set_test_devices`** (write, `PUT /api/v1/rcs/agents/:id/test-devices`)
  Replace the RCS agent's test-device list — the phones that can receive messages from the agent while it's in the 'testing' stage (send_rcs reaches invited devices only until the agent is live). The list is authoritative: numbers missing from it are removed and new ones are invited, up to 20. phoneNumber accepts E.164 (+13125550100) or a 10-digit US number. Returns { devices } with each device's inviteStatus (null until the invite has gone out). rcs_field_locked (409) while the agent is awaiting review or a launch is requested; rcs_not_found when the ID isn't in this workspace. Requires the rcs:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`rcs_submit_registration`** (write, `POST /api/v1/rcs/agents/:id/submit`)
  Submit the RCS brand and agent to Sendly for review — step 3, and where completeness is enforced. On success agent.reviewStatus becomes 'awaiting_review' (stage 'in_review'), the brand goes with it, both lock, and Sendly is notified. What happens next: Sendly reviews the registration and either asks for changes (stage 'changes_requested' — the account is emailed; read reviewNote, fix with rcs_update_brand / rcs_update_agent, then submit again) or sends it to the carrier network, which verifies the brand ('brand_verification') and reviews the agent ('agent_review') before the agent reaches 'testing'. Poll rcs_get_agent or rcs_get_registration for the stage. Errors: rcs_invalid_content lists every missing or invalid field as errors[].path ('brand.ein', 'agent.logoUrl', 'agent.contacts', ...) — fix them all, then retry; rcs_field_locked (409) when it has already been submitted or the brand was rejected; rcs_brand_not_verified (409) when the carrier network failed the brand; rcs_not_found when the ID isn't in this workspace. Requires the rcs:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.
- **`rcs_request_launch`** (write, `POST /api/v1/rcs/agents/:id/request-launch`)
  Ask Sendly to launch the RCS agent to every RCS-capable recipient — the final step, available once the agent is in the 'testing' stage (agent.reviewStatus 'approved_for_carrier', or 'launch_rejected' to try again). Before calling: invite a phone with rcs_set_test_devices, send it a message with send_rcs, record a short screen video of that message arriving with the agent name visible, host it somewhere reviewers can open it (an unlisted video link works), and pass the https:// link as testUrl; make sure the campaign is complete via rcs_update_agent. On success agent.reviewStatus becomes 'launch_requested' (stage 'launch_review') and Sendly is notified; Sendly reviews the launch and sends it to the carrier network ('launching'), after which the agent is 'live' — poll rcs_get_agent. Errors: rcs_launch_not_ready (409) when the agent isn't in testing yet; rcs_invalid_content with errors[].path under 'campaign.…' / 'testing.…' for what's missing (companyOverview, agentOverview, at least 1 interaction, at least 3 messageExamples, consentSettings, testUrl); rcs_field_locked (409) when a launch is already requested; rcs_not_found when the ID isn't in this workspace. Requires the rcs:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit verification changes.

## Short codes

4 tools.

- **`short_codes_get_application`** (read-only, `GET /api/v1/short_codes/application`)
  Get the workspace's short code application — a 5 or 6 digit US sender, which is applied for rather than bought. Returns the application, whether it is still editable (and lockMessage saying why not), the carrier forms it needs with requiredDocuments / missingDocuments / documents, the quoted monthly lease (quote.monthlyUsd, never charged automatically), and carriers with how many of the four have approved. Start here. reviewStatus says what happens next: 'draft' — fill it in with short_codes_update_application, check with short_codes_check_application, then short_codes_submit_application; 'awaiting_review' — Sendly is reviewing it, nothing to do; 'changes_requested' — read application.reviewNote, fix, submit again; 'approved_for_filing' — Sendly emails the carrier forms to the contact on the application to sign, and documents[].signedAt tracks them; 'filed' — with the carriers, who certify independently over several weeks; 'rejected' — read reviewNote, then start again. status is the code itself: 'requested', 'provisioning', 'parked' (assigned but not cleared to send), 'active' (sendable), 'suspended', 'cancelled'. Only 'active' can send. Error short_codes_not_enabled means short codes aren't enabled for this account yet — the account owner can ask Sendly support. Read-only; requires the short_codes:read scope.
- **`short_codes_update_application`** (write, `PUT /api/v1/short_codes/application`)
  Save answers on the short code application, creating it on the first call. Pass only what you know; call it again to fill the rest. US carriers require, before it can be submitted: useCase, optInFlow, a precise messageFrequency (for example '4 messages per month', not 'occasionally'), helpResponse and stopConfirmation that meet the keyword rules, privacyPolicyUrl and termsUrl, and the Short Code Registry contact (brandContactName, brandContactEmail). campaignKeyword is the word subscribers text to join, and optInConfirmation is what they get back. Fields Sendly or the carriers own — the digits, status, reviewStatus, carrier approvals — cannot be set here and come back named in ignoredFields. Returns the saved application. Error short_code_locked (409) once the application is with Sendly or the carriers; the reply says which. Requires the short_codes:write scope; on non-personal workspaces the key's role must permit settings changes.
- **`short_codes_check_application`** (read-only, `POST /api/v1/short_codes/application/preflight`)
  Check the short code application against the carrier rules without changing anything. Returns ok, issues (each with the field path and what is wrong), and the carrier forms still outstanding. Call this before short_codes_submit_application and fix everything it names — the same checks run at submit and reject it otherwise. Read-only; requires the short_codes:read scope.
- **`short_codes_submit_application`** (write, `POST /api/v1/short_codes/application/submit`)
  Submit the short code application to Sendly for review — the last step an agent can take. On success reviewStatus becomes 'awaiting_review' and Sendly is notified; from there a human reviews it, Sendly emails the carrier forms to the contact on the application to sign, files it, and each carrier certifies the code separately over several weeks. Submitting twice is safe: the second call returns alreadySubmitted true and changes nothing. Errors: short_code_invalid_application (422) with errors[] naming every field still wrong — fix with short_codes_update_application and submit again; short_code_ai_draft_unedited (422) when suggested wording was never edited by a person; short_code_locked (409) when it is already with Sendly or the carriers. Requires the short_codes:write scope.
